label: Error Handling
summary: Modern SSL error handling with TRY/CATCH/FINALLY and error retrieval.
must_follow: :TRY requires at least one of :CATCH or :FINALLY; a bare :TRY ... :ENDTRY is invalid.
Use GetLastSSLError() inside :CATCH to retrieve error details.

Check an envelope's success flag before reading its payload; validate the envelope's shape and the payload's field types only when the result comes from a separately deployed script or service without a documented contract, never for a procedure in the same file.

Assign each invariant to one authoritative boundary; repeat a check downstream only when it protects a distinct local use, enforces a stronger invariant, receives independently supplied data, or defends an independently deployed public contract.
Catch an error only to roll back or finish work, to return a failure result a caller branches on, or to add context the error lacks; otherwise let it propagate to the boundary that owns it.
avoid: Do not assume UsrMes, ErrorMes, or InfoMes displays messages to users; they are server log functions.

Do not check for a state the code already rules out: a parameter every caller passes, a type SSL or the producer guarantees, a value already checked upstream, or the result of a procedure in the same file.

elements.name: TRY
elements.summary: Starts a protected block that can transfer control to :CATCH, :FINALLY, or both when errors occur.

elements.name: CATCH
elements.summary: Handles errors raised in the immediately preceding :TRY block.

elements.name: FINALLY
elements.summary: Starts the cleanup section of a :TRY block and always runs after the protected work completes.

elements.name: ENDTRY
elements.summary: Closes a structured :TRY block after its :CATCH and/or :FINALLY sections.

elements.name: GetLastSSLError
elements.summary: Retrieves the most recent SSL error encountered during the current process.

elements.name: ClearLastSSLError
elements.summary: Clears the stored SSL error so later error checks start clean.

elements.name: ErrorMes
elements.summary: Writes an error message to the server log, even when user-message logging is disabled, and returns the formatted log entry.
